title: Characterization of Right Ventricular Function in Cardiogenic Shock with Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation
summary:
Cardiogenic shock is the most severe and life-threatening form of acute heart failure. Due to the markedly impaired pumping function of the heart, vital organs are no longer adequately supplied with blood and oxygen. Common causes include acute myocardial infarction, severe valvular heart disease, or inflammation of the heart muscle.

In addition to early treatment of the underlying cause of acute heart failure, stabilization of the cardiovascular system is the primary goal in order to restore oxygen supply to vital organs. If pharmacological therapy is insufficient, mechanical circulatory support may be used, most commonly in the form of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Although this approach often achieves short-term stabilization, current studies have not yet demonstrated a survival benefit of this therapy.¹²

Previous investigations of cardiogenic shock under ECMO therapy have mainly focused on the left ventricle. However, in recent years it has become evident that the function of the right ventricle also has a decisive impact on prognosis in various disease settings.³⁴ Its role in cardiogenic shock during mechanical circulatory support remains insufficiently studied, despite mechanistic considerations suggesting that it may particularly benefit.

The CHARGE-ECLS study therefore aims to systematically investigate right ventricular function in cardiogenic shock during ECMO therapy. A better understanding of the effects of shock on both ventricles may enable more targeted and individualized control of ECMO therapy in the future. This has the potential to improve recovery and possibly also the prognosis of these critically ill patients.

Cardiac function can be most accurately described by simultaneously recording pressure and volume changes throughout the cardiac cycle. Using specialized catheters, such pressure–volume loops can be obtained, allowing for a detailed characterization of cardiac function.⁵

Within the CHARGE-ECLS study, these measurements are performed in the right ventricle under different ECMO settings while simultaneously assessing pressures in the pulmonary circulation. This approach aims to comprehensively characterize right ventricular function in cardiogenic shock. The insights gained are intended to help identify patient-specific settings for mechanical circulatory support, with the goal of improving survival in this still highly critical condition.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cardiogenic shock with a clinical indication for VA-ECMO therapy
Age > 18 years
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient hemodynamic stability despite established VA-ECMO therapy to safely perform study procedures
Lack of the possibility to obtain safe venous vascular access
Patients with an implanted pacemaker or transvenous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD)
Patients younger than 18 years of age
Presence of pregnancy and other particularly vulnerable populations
Conditions that make it impossible to obtain informed consent from a legal representative for study participation
